chapters.title: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
chapters.summary: Trace the emergence of the nation-state and national identity in nineteenth-century Europe.
chapters.source_reference: NCERT India and the Contemporary World-II, Chapter 1, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

topics.title: The French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation

lessons.title: How the Nation Was Imagined
lessons.summary: Understand how revolutionary France created symbols of collective identity.
learning_objectives: Describe two measures that created a sense of collective identity

content_blocks.text: The French Revolution transferred sovereignty from a monarch to citizens. New flags, hymns and uniform laws helped imagine France as a nation.
The tricolour flag replaced the royal standard and became a visual symbol of the new nation.
National identity is built through shared symbols, rights and institutions.

concepts.title: Popular sovereignty
concepts.explanation: The idea that authority rests with the people rather than a hereditary ruler.

lessons.source_reference: NCERT India and the Contemporary World-II, Chapter 1, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.prompt: Which flag became a symbol of revolutionary France?
questions.explanation: The blue-white-red tricolour replaced the royal standard.

topics.title: The Making of Nationalism in Europe

lessons.title: The Making of Nationalism in Europe
lessons.summary: Trace how language, culture and romanticism shaped national identity after 1848.
prerequisites: The French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation

content_blocks.text: After Napoleon, nationalism grew through shared language, folklore and culture. Romantics argued that true national spirit lived in the people's customs rather than in dynasties.
Germany: folk songs, fairy tales and the German language became tools of national awakening before unification in 1871.
Culture and language can unite scattered peoples into one imagined nation.

concepts.title: Romanticism
concepts.explanation: A cultural movement that glorified folk tradition and emotion as the basis of national identity.

lessons.source_reference: NCERT India and the Contemporary World-II, Chapter 1, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.prompt: How did romanticism help in the making of nationalism in Europe?
questions.answer: Romantic artists and writers used folk culture, language and emotion to evoke a shared national spirit.
questions.explanation: By glorifying vernacular cultures, romanticism gave scattered communities a common identity.

chapters.title: Resources and Development
chapters.summary: Classify resources and understand sustainable planning and land use.

lessons.title: How Resources Are Classified
lessons.summary: Classify resources by origin, exhaustibility, ownership and status of development.
learning_objectives: Explain why planning is needed for sustainable development

content_blocks.text: Resources may be classified by origin, exhaustibility, ownership and status of development. The same resource can belong to more than one category.
Solar energy is a renewable, biotic? No: abiotic resource, and may be community or national depending on the context of use.
Resource planning balances current needs with conservation for future generations.

concepts.title: Sustainable development
concepts.explanation: Development that meets present needs without compromising future generations.

questions.prompt: Why is resource planning essential in India?
questions.answer: Resources are unevenly distributed and need judicious use for sustainable development.
questions.explanation: Planning addresses unequal distribution, technology and conservation.

lessons.title: Land Use and Resource Planning in India
lessons.summary: Analyse land-use patterns and the steps of national resource planning.
learning_objectives: Explain the four steps of resource planning

content_blocks.text: Land use in India is dominated by net sown area, forests and land not available for cultivation. Resource planning works in four steps: identifying, inventorying, matching with development, and evolving a plan.
Wasteland can be reclaimed with appropriate technology, while forest land is conserved to check degradation.
Planning matches available resources to development needs without exhausting them.

concepts.title: Land use
concepts.explanation: How the total land area of a country is distributed among its different uses.

questions.prompt: Suggest two ways to reduce the degradation of land under forest cover in India.
questions.answer: Regulated grazing, afforestation, and community-based forest management reduce degradation.
questions.explanation: Sustainable use keeps forest land productive for future generations.
